descriptors.statement: Death and Hades are abolished, thrown into the lake of fire, so that death no longer has any place.
Abraham is present and recognizable in heaven, conversing with those there.
The righteous dead are gathered to Abraham's side, in the company of the patriarchs.
Death will be no more in the new creation.
There will be no more mourning, crying, or pain, for the former things will have passed away.
In the new creation, the sea will be no more.
Violence, devastation, and destruction are no longer heard within the city.
All the people of God are righteous and possess the land forever.
God, seated on the throne, declares that he is making all things new.
Believers will always be with the Lord.
The four living creatures say 'Amen!' and the elders fall down and worship.
The clothing of the Ancient of Days is white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The purity, holiness, and eternal age of God depicted in apocalyptic imagery.

descriptors.statement: Angels carry believers at death to their place of blessing.
Innumerable angels are gathered in festal assembly in the heavenly city.
Angels descend from heaven with authority over the bottomless pit.
All the angels stand around the throne, around the elders, and around the four living creatures, falling on their faces to worship God.
Angels identify themselves as fellow servants with believers who hold the testimony of Jesus.
Angels dwell in heaven.
Angels in heaven refuse worship, directing it instead to God alone.
Demons recognize that there is an appointed time at which they will be tormented.
The armies of heaven follow Christ on white horses, arrayed in fine linen, white and pure.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The heavenly host (angels and/or glorified saints) accompanying Christ in his triumph.

descriptors.statement: The assembly of the firstborn are enrolled in heaven.
While at home in the body, the believer is away from the Lord.
To be away from the body is to be at home with the Lord.
God's servants will see his face.
The pure in heart shall see God.
The redeemed will visibly behold the glory of the LORD.
Believers who have died are described as asleep, awaiting the Lord's coming.
The faithful endured suffering in hope of resurrection to a better life.
Those who share in the first resurrection are blessed and holy, and the second death has no power over them.
The book of life is opened before God's throne and contains the names of those who belong to him.
The new Jerusalem is called the Bride, the wife of the Lamb.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The redeemed people of God (the Church) and/or the city that houses them, in covenant union with Christ.

descriptors.statement: The Bride of the Lamb has made herself ready for the marriage.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The redeemed church prepared for union with Christ.

descriptors.statement: Those gathered into the kingdom feast are called, but only those chosen are finally received.
Living believers will be caught up together with the resurrected dead in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air.
The four living creatures ceaselessly proclaim day and night, 'Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come.'
The Christ, David's Lord, is seated at the right hand of God until his enemies are made his footstool.
Christ's eyes are like a flame of fire.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Christ's penetrating, omniscient judgment that sees and consumes all evil.

descriptors.statement: Christ judges and makes war in righteousness.
Christ himself is present with believers in heaven.
Christ has the power to subject all things to himself, by which he will transform believers' bodies.
Christ has a name written that no one knows but himself.
Christ wears many diadems on his head.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Christ's comprehensive royal sovereignty over all kingdoms.

descriptors.statement: Christ must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
The citizenship of believers is in heaven.
The city has no need of sun or moon, for the glory of God gives it light, and its lamp is the Lamb.
The city is called the City of the LORD, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
God has prepared a city for those who desire the heavenly country, and he is not ashamed to be called their God.
Heaven includes a city with foundations, designed and built by God, which the patriarchs anticipated by faith.
Believers in heaven are comforted after the sufferings of this life.
Above the heads of the living creatures is an expanse shining like awe-inspiring crystal.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The platform or firmament that separates God's throne above from the created order below, signifying his transcendence

descriptors.statement: The dead in Christ will rise first at the Lord's coming.
Death will be swallowed up in victory.
Believers who have died will be brought with Jesus at his coming.
Those whose names are written in the book of life are spared from the lake of fire.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
Resurrected believers will differ in glory, as star differs from star in glory.
The LORD will comfort his people as a mother comforts her child.
The glory of God dwells in his sanctuary, filling it with his presence.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The manifest presence of God filling his eternal dwelling place with his people

descriptors.statement: There is a door standing open in heaven through which John is invited to ascend.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Access granted to John for prophetic vision of the heavenly realm

descriptors.statement: From the presence of God on the throne, earth and sky flee away and no place is found for them.
The earth shines with the glory of God when he comes.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The illumination of the renewed creation by God's manifest presence

descriptors.statement: Days of mourning are ended for God's people.
The offspring and name of the LORD's people will remain enduringly before him, just as the new heavens and new earth remain.
Enoch was taken up by God so that he did not see death, having pleased God by faith.
Seated above the throne is a figure with a human appearance, whose form is like gleaming metal and fire with brightness all around.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The visible appearance of the glory of the LORD, manifested in human-like form upon his throne

descriptors.statement: Only those whose righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees enter the kingdom of heaven.
Believers have an eternal dwelling from God in the heavens, not made with hands.
The believer's heavenly dwelling is eternal.
God makes his city majestic forever, a joy from age to age.
God's people rejoice forever in what he creates.
The kingdom given to the saints is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.
Outside the city are dogs, sorcerers, the sexually immoral, murderers, idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.
Christ, the rider on the white horse, is called Faithful and True.
The Father dwells in heaven.
The heavenly Father is perfect.
The Father and the Son make their home with those who love Jesus and keep his word.
Heaven is the Father's house.
The Bride is clothed in fine linen, bright and pure, which represents the righteous deeds of the saints.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The righteous deeds of the saints, explicitly identified by the text.

descriptors.statement: Fire comes down from heaven to consume the enemies of the saints.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: God's decisive judgment from his heavenly throne against the final assault on his people.

descriptors.statement: The hearts of God's servants will rejoice and their bones will flourish like grass.
In the new creation the former things shall not be remembered or come into mind.
Four living creatures, full of eyes in front and behind, are positioned around the throne on each side.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Exalted angelic beings (cherubim-like) representing creation worshiping God

descriptors.statement: The four living creatures resemble respectively a lion, an ox, a man, and an eagle in flight.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The fullness of God's created order represented before His throne

descriptors.statement: Each of the four living creatures has six wings and is covered with eyes all around and within.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Angelic readiness, comprehensive vigilance, and perception in service to God

descriptors.statement: Four living creatures are present around the throne.
Four living creatures attend the divine throne, each having four faces (human, lion, ox, eagle) and four wings.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Angelic beings (cherubim) who attend and bear the throne of God, representing the fullness of created life serving the Creator

descriptors.statement: The sound of the wings of the living creatures is like the sound of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, like the tumult of an army.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The overwhelming majesty and power associated with the heavenly beings who attend God

descriptors.statement: Four living creatures are present in heaven before the throne of God.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: High-ranking angelic beings who attend God's throne and lead heavenly worship.

descriptors.statement: The city is laid out as a foursquare, with its length, width, and height equal, measuring 12,000 stadia.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The perfection and completeness of God's dwelling place, evoking the cubic Holy of Holies; the entire city is a sanctuary.

descriptors.statement: The gates of the city will never be shut by day, and there will be no night there.
The twelve gates of the city are twelve pearls, each gate made of a single pearl.
Christ will transform the lowly bodies of believers to be like his glorious body.
The glory and honor of the nations will be brought into the city.
The holy city Jerusalem has the glory of God, with radiance like a most rare jewel, like jasper, clear as crystal.
The glory of the LORD rises upon and is seen upon his redeemed city.
The vision Ezekiel sees is the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD.
When all things are subjected to Christ, the Son himself will also be subjected to the Father, that God may be all in all.
God identifies himself as the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end.
God answers his people before they call and hears while they are yet speaking.
God is the glory of his people.
God's dwelling place will be with man, and he will dwell with them as their God, and they will be his people.
God dwells in the midst of his people forever.
The redeemed will need no light of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will be their light.
God is the God of the living, not of the dead; Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are alive to him.
God himself rejoices in Jerusalem and is glad in his people.
God rewards those who earnestly seek him.
God, the judge of all, is present in the heavenly assembly.
God now warns from heaven.
God is a consuming fire.
God will wipe away every tear from the eyes of the redeemed.
God will wipe away every tear from the eyes of his people.
God's judgments are declared in heaven to be true and just.
God's name will be on the foreheads of his servants.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The redeemed belong to God and are identified as his own.

descriptors.statement: God beautifies his house and makes the place of his feet glorious.
He who sits on the throne shelters the redeemed with his presence.
God's throne is the central location around which angels, elders, living creatures, and the redeemed are gathered.
God's sanctuary is the place of his throne, where he dwells in the midst of his people forever.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: God's eternal dwelling with his redeemed people

descriptors.statement: The twenty-four elders hold harps and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: the prayers of the saints, explicitly identified in the text

descriptors.statement: In the kingdom of heaven there are gradations: some will be called least and some great, according to their relation to God's commandments.
A great impassable chasm separates the place of the righteous from the place of the wicked dead, so that none may cross between them.
A great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, tribe, people, and language, stands before God's throne and before the Lamb.
A great multitude in heaven cries out praise to God, saying 'Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God.'
Heaven opens to reveal Christ riding forth on a white horse.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The unveiling of Christ's coming forth in judgment and conquest.

descriptors.statement: Heaven is the throne of God.
The homeland the faithful seek is a heavenly country, better than any earthly land.
The heavenly court sits in judgment, and the books are opened.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The divine judgment scene in which God adjudicates the deeds of nations and persons recorded in his books.

descriptors.statement: A thousand thousands serve God, and ten thousand times ten thousand stand before him.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The innumerable angelic attendants who serve and worship God in his heavenly court.

descriptors.statement: Believers have come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem.
Moses considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt because he looked to the heavenly reward.
Thrones are set in place in the heavenly court.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The throne room of God where divine judgment is rendered; the seats of authority surrounding God's own throne.

descriptors.statement: God's holy name is no longer defiled in his eternal dwelling.
The whole territory of God's holy mountain is most holy.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The pervasive holiness of God's eternal dwelling, the heavenly Mount Zion

descriptors.statement: Resurrected believers will bear the image of the man of heaven (Christ).
The mortal body will put on immortality.
The one who conquers will inherit these things, and God will be his God and he will be God's son.
The wall of the city is built of jasper, while the city itself is pure gold, like clear glass.
Jesus is seated at the right hand of the throne of God.
Jesus is the mediator of a new covenant in the heavenly assembly.
Jesus has gone to prepare a place in the Father's house for his disciples.
Jesus is the only way to come to the Father.
All believers must appear before the judgment seat of Christ to receive what is due for what was done in the body.
Christ bears the name 'King of kings and Lord of lords' on his robe and on his thigh.
At the end, Christ will deliver the kingdom to God the Father after destroying every rule, authority, and power.
Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
The kingdom of heaven includes Gentiles from east and west, not only ethnic Israelites.
The kingdom of heaven belongs to the poor in spirit.
The kingdom of heaven belongs to those persecuted for righteousness' sake.
The dominion of the Son of Man is everlasting and shall not pass away, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed.
The Lamb is present with God on the throne in the eternal city.
No one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or look into it except the Lamb.
The Lamb in the midst of the throne will be the shepherd of the redeemed.
The Lamb is worshiped together with him who sits on the throne, receiving equal praise.
Between the throne and the four living creatures and the elders stands a Lamb appearing as though it had been slain.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Jesus Christ, the crucified and risen Savior, retaining the marks of his sacrificial death

descriptors.statement: The Lamb takes the scroll from the right hand of him who is seated on the throne.
Only those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will enter the city.
At the last trumpet, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, the dead will be raised imperishable and the living will be changed.
The leaves of the tree of life are for the healing of the nations.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The full and ongoing wholeness God provides to the redeemed peoples.

descriptors.statement: Because Jesus lives, his disciples also will live.
Those in the resurrection are like the angels in heaven.
Jesus is identified in heaven as the Lion of the tribe of Judah and the Root of David, who has conquered.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Jesus Christ as the messianic conqueror from Judah's line and David's lineage

descriptors.statement: The sun and moon no longer give light, for the LORD himself is the everlasting light of his people.
The Lord himself will descend from heaven with a cry of command, the voice of an archangel, and the trumpet of God.
The Father's house contains many rooms.
The marriage of the Lamb takes place, uniting Christ with his Bride.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The consummated union of Christ with his redeemed church.

descriptors.statement: Those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb are blessed.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The consummated joyful fellowship between Christ and his redeemed people in the eternal state.

descriptors.statement: Many will come from east and west to recline at table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
A mighty angel proclaims with a loud voice in heaven.
What is mortal in the believer will be swallowed up by life.
The heavenly Jerusalem is identified with Mount Zion and the city of the living God.
Around the throne and the living creatures and the elders are many angels numbering myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands.
The names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel are inscribed on the gates of the city.
Nations and kings come to the light of God's people.
The nations will walk by the light of the city, and the kings of the earth will bring their glory into it.
There will be a new heaven and a new earth, replacing the first heaven and first earth which will have passed away.
God creates new heavens and a new earth.
The LORD will make new heavens and a new earth that shall remain before him.
Believers await new heavens and a new earth, promised by God, in which righteousness dwells.
The holy city, the new Jerusalem, will come down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
God creates Jerusalem to be a joy and her people to be a gladness.
The four living creatures and elders sing a new song declaring the Lamb worthy because he was slain and by his blood ransomed people for God from every tribe, language, people, and nation.
None shall hurt or destroy on God's holy mountain.
The redeemed shall hunger no more and thirst no more.
In the resurrection, people neither marry nor are given in marriage.
Nothing accursed will exist there any longer.
The sound of weeping and the cry of distress shall no more be heard in the new Jerusalem.
There will be no night there.
The sun shall not strike the redeemed, nor any scorching heat.
There is no temple in the city, for its temple is the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb.
Nothing unclean, and no one who does what is detestable or false, will ever enter the city.
The one seated on the throne has the appearance of jasper and carnelian.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: God the Father's radiant glory and majesty

descriptors.statement: God who sits on the throne lives forever and ever.
The gates of the city stand open continually, never shut day or night.
The heavens can be opened to grant a human visions of God.
The redeemed multitude comes out of the great tribulation.
Those excluded from the kingdom are cast into outer darkness, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: the place of final exclusion from God's kingdom, i.e., final judgment/hell, contrasted with the lighted banquet hall

descriptors.statement: Heaven is called 'paradise.'
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are present in the kingdom of heaven.
The wolf and the lamb graze together, and the lion eats straw like the ox.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: the comprehensive peace and absence of predation/violence in God's renewed creation

descriptors.statement: Peace governs the city and righteousness oversees it.
Peace will flow to God's people like a river.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: the abundant, unceasing peace God grants his redeemed people

descriptors.statement: The Old Testament faithful did not receive the promised reward in this life, because God planned that they would be made perfect together with New Covenant believers.
Believers will be with Jesus in the place where he is.
The LORD will take some from the gathered nations to serve as priests and Levites.
There is a prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus for which believers press on.
The new heavens and new earth are the fulfillment of God's own promise.
The brightness surrounding the enthroned figure is like the appearance of the rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The covenant glory and beauty surrounding God's throne, recalling the Noahic covenant sign

descriptors.statement: A rainbow with the appearance of an emerald encircles the throne.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: God's covenant faithfulness surrounding His rule

descriptors.statement: The redeemed are made a kingdom and priests to God and shall reign on the earth.
The redeemed will reign forever and ever.
The Lord God the Almighty reigns, and his reign is proclaimed in heaven.
The new heavens and new earth come after the present heavens and earth are dissolved by fire on the day of the Lord.
The resurrection body differs from the natural body as a plant differs from the seed sown.
The resurrection body is raised imperishable.
The resurrection body is raised in glory.
The resurrection body is raised in power.
The resurrection body is raised a spiritual body.
The believer's hope includes attaining the resurrection from the dead.
All who belong to Christ will be made alive at his coming.
Christ has been raised from the dead as the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
Those persecuted and reviled on account of Christ have a great reward in heaven.
Those who wash their robes have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by the gates.
Righteousness dwells in the new heavens and new earth.
A river of life-giving water flows out from the sanctuary of God.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The life-giving presence of God flowing out from his throne, fulfilled in the river of the water of life in the New Jerusalem (Rev 22:1-2).

descriptors.statement: The river flowing from God's sanctuary grows deeper and more powerful the further it goes.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The expanding and unstoppable life-giving presence of God going out from his dwelling.

descriptors.statement: Wherever the river from God's sanctuary flows, it brings life and healing, making even salt waters fresh.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The life-giving and restorative effect of God's presence on creation.

descriptors.statement: A stream of fire issues and comes out from before the Ancient of Days.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The outflowing judgment and holiness of God proceeding from his presence.

descriptors.statement: A river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The life-giving presence and Spirit that proceed from God and the Lamb to sustain the redeemed.

descriptors.statement: Christ is clothed in a robe dipped in blood.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Christ as warrior-judge, marked either by his atoning blood or by the blood of his vanquished enemies.

descriptors.statement: The redeemed have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Cleansing from sin and justification through Christ's atoning sacrifice

descriptors.statement: Christ rules the nations with a rod of iron.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: Christ's unbreakable, sovereign rule over the nations.

descriptors.statement: Those who belong to Christ serve as priests of God and of Christ.
The saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom and possess it forever, forever and ever.
Judgment is given for the saints of the Most High, and the time comes when the saints possess the kingdom.
The kingdom and the dominion and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High.
The redeemed cry out in worship, 'Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!'
The sanctuary of the LORD stands in the midst of the holy portion of the land.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: God's dwelling at the center of his people's life in the eschaton; ultimately fulfilled in God and the Lamb as the temple of the New Jerusalem (cf. Rev 21:22).

descriptors.statement: Believers await the Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, to come from heaven.
Before the throne is what appears to be a sea of glass, like crystal.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The transcendent holiness and serene separation of God from creation

descriptors.statement: He who is seated on the throne holds in his right hand a scroll written within and on the back, sealed with seven seals.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: God's sovereign plan/decree for redemption and judgment, held in his authoritative right hand

descriptors.statement: Holiness is necessary to see the Lord.
God's servants will worship him there.
The redeemed serve God day and night in his temple.
The Lamb has seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: the Lamb's complete power (horns) and omniscience (eyes), associated with the sevenfold Spirit of God

descriptors.statement: Seven torches of fire burn before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The Holy Spirit in His fullness/sevenfold perfection

descriptors.statement: Angels ascribe blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and might to God forever and ever.
The angels declare with a loud voice that the Lamb who was slain is worthy to receive power, wealth, wisdom, might, honor, glory, and blessing.
God has promised to shake not only the earth but also the heavens once more.
The final shaking will remove created things that can be shaken so that the unshakable things remain.
One like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven and is presented before the Ancient of Days.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The exaltation of Christ, who ascends to the Father and is enthroned at his right hand.

descriptors.statement: The Son of Man is given dominion, glory, and a kingdom, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him.
Peacemakers shall be called sons of God.
Those who love their enemies show themselves to be sons of their Father in heaven.
The voice of the heavenly multitude sounds like the roar of many waters and like mighty peals of thunder.
God has given the Holy Spirit to believers as a guarantee of their heavenly dwelling.
The spirits of the righteous have been made perfect in the heavenly assembly.
To the thirsty, God will give from the spring of the water of life without payment.
The Lamb will guide the redeemed to springs of living water.
The sprinkled blood of Jesus speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
Believers on earth are strangers and exiles, their true home lying elsewhere.
The street of the city is pure gold, like transparent glass.
The river flows through the middle of the street of the city.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The civic life of the New Jerusalem, ordered around God's life-giving presence.

descriptors.statement: A sharp sword comes from Christ's mouth with which he strikes down the nations.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The judicial power of Christ's word by which he conquers and judges his enemies.

descriptors.statement: Jesus will return and take his disciples to himself so that they may be where he is.
The name of the eschatological city is 'The LORD Is There,' signifying God's permanent presence with his people in it.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The defining reality of the New Jerusalem: God himself dwells with his people there (cf. Rev 21:3).

descriptors.statement: The city has three gates on each of the four sides: east, north, south, and west.
A throne stands in heaven with one seated upon it.
Flashes of lightning, rumblings, and peals of thunder come from the throne.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: God's awesome power and theophanic majesty proceeding from His throne

descriptors.statement: The throne of God is the place at whose right hand Christ is seated.
Heaven is the throne of the LORD.
Above the crystal expanse there is the likeness of a throne in appearance like sapphire.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: God's sovereign rule, depicted as a sapphire throne above the heavenly expanse

descriptors.statement: The throne of the Ancient of Days is fiery flames, and its wheels are burning fire.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The holiness and consuming judgment of God depicted as a fiery throne in apocalyptic vision.

descriptors.statement: God is seated on a throne in heaven.
The throne of God and of the Lamb is in the city.
The twenty-four elders and four living creatures fall down and worship God who is seated on the throne.
The tree of life grows on either side of the river, bearing twelve kinds of fruit and yielding its fruit each month.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The restored access to eternal life granted to the redeemed in God's presence.

descriptors.statement: Trees bearing fruit every month grow on the banks of the river that flows from God's sanctuary, with leaves for healing.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The tree of life imagery fulfilled in Rev 22:2 — perpetual fruitfulness and healing flowing from God's presence.

descriptors.statement: The fruit of the trees on the river banks never fails and their leaves never wither, because the water nourishing them flows from the sanctuary of God.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The unfailing sustenance and life that proceeds from God's presence.

descriptors.statement: The wall of the city has twelve foundations, on which are inscribed the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
The eschatological city has twelve gates named after the twelve tribes of Israel, three on each of its four sides.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The gates of the New Jerusalem named for the twelve tribes of Israel, signifying that the people of God in their fullness have access to the city (cf. Rev 21:12-13).

descriptors.statement: The city has a great, high wall with twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels.
The foundations of the wall of the city are adorned with twelve kinds of jewels: jasper, sapphire, agate, emerald, onyx, carnelian, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprase, jacinth, and amethyst.
Twenty-four elders sit on twenty-four thrones around God's throne, clothed in white garments and wearing golden crowns.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The redeemed people of God (possibly representing the twelve tribes and twelve apostles) reigning with Christ

descriptors.statement: The twenty-four elders fall down before the one seated on the throne and worship him, casting their crowns before the throne.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The redeemed offering all honor and authority back to God

descriptors.statement: Twenty-four elders are present around the throne.
Twenty-four elders are present in heaven before the throne of God.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The full company of God's redeemed people represented in heavenly council before God's throne.

descriptors.statement: Every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea ascribes blessing, honor, glory, and might to him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb forever and ever.
Believers receive a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
God gives the redeemed victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
God has avenged the blood of his servants by judging the great prostitute.
A voice from the throne summons all God's servants, small and great, to praise him.
The wall of the city measures 144 cubits by human measurement, which is also an angel's measurement.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The squared number of the tribes/apostles (12x12), signifying the completeness of God's people.

descriptors.statement: The walls of the city are called Salvation and its gates Praise.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The protective boundaries of God's people are constituted by his salvation, and access to his presence is constituted by praise.

descriptors.statement: The water of life is offered without price to the one who is thirsty.
The wealth of the nations is brought into God's city.
The kingdom of heaven is likened to a wedding feast that a king gives for his son.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The consummated joy of the kingdom of heaven, in which God the Father celebrates the union of his Son with his redeemed people.

descriptors.statement: Entry into the wedding feast of the kingdom requires a wedding garment; those without one are cast out into outer darkness.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The righteousness required to be received into the kingdom — the imputed righteousness of Christ clothing the believer.

descriptors.statement: Gleaming wheels like beryl, constructed as wheel within wheel, accompany the living creatures, with rims full of eyes all around.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The mobility and omniscient vigilance of God's throne, which goes in every direction and sees all things

descriptors.statement: The spirit of the living creatures is in the wheels, so that wheels and creatures move and stop in perfect concert.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The unified, Spirit-directed motion of God's heavenly throne and its attendants

descriptors.statement: The redeemed multitude is clothed in white robes and holds palm branches.
Believers are with Christ in heaven immediately upon death.
Christ is called The Word of God.
God's people are the work of his hands, planted by him for his glory.
Those in heaven ascribe salvation, glory, and power to God.
The four living creatures and twenty-four elders fall down before the Lamb in worship.
The elders declare that the Lord God is worthy to receive glory, honor, and power because He created all things and by His will they existed and were created.
